meaning.objective: Identify row/column order and valid matrix dimensions without a supplied definition.
misconceptions: reversing rows and columns
confusing the number of entries with matrix dimensions

application.objective: Compute one entry of a product of two small compatible matrices, using nontrivial integers.
misconceptions: multiplying entries element by element
using a row from each factor instead of a row and column

reasoning.objective: Select a valid reason or explicit counterexample showing that matrix multiplication need not commute.
misconceptions: assuming scalar commutativity transfers to matrices
assuming equal dimensions force equal products

meaning.objective: Identify vector equality from ordered components and distinguish position from magnitude.
misconceptions: same magnitude implies equal vectors
component order is irrelevant

application.objective: Compute a small linear combination of two vectors with signed scalar coefficients.
misconceptions: forgetting a negative coefficient
adding the scalar to each component

reasoning.objective: Judge whether a proposed vector lies in the span of two specified vectors and choose a valid justification.
misconceptions: any vector in the ambient space lies in the span
matching only one component proves membership

meaning.objective: Distinguish no solution, one solution, and infinitely many solutions of a linear system.
misconceptions: a free variable means no solution
every square system has exactly one solution

application.objective: Find the solution of a concrete two-variable linear system with a unique solution.
misconceptions: sign error during elimination
substituting into only one original equation

reasoning.objective: Infer consistency from an augmented row-echelon matrix and select the valid reason.
misconceptions: ignoring a contradictory augmented row
confusing a free variable with inconsistency

meaning.objective: Recognize the condition that defines linear independence using the zero linear combination.
misconceptions: no vector is zero implies independence
distinct vectors are always independent

application.objective: Determine dependence of a small explicit vector set by finding a nontrivial linear combination.
misconceptions: checking only vector inequality
treating the zero coefficient solution as evidence of dependence

reasoning.objective: Judge a dependence claim for more than two vectors and identify a valid argument or counterexample.
misconceptions: pairwise nonparallel implies joint independence
independence of a subset guarantees independence of the full set

meaning.objective: Identify both spanning and linear independence as necessary conditions for a basis of a specified space.
misconceptions: spanning alone is sufficient
linear independence alone is sufficient regardless of size

application.objective: Find coordinates of a vector relative to a specified nonstandard basis in R^2.
misconceptions: using standard coordinates as basis coordinates
swapping the order of the basis vectors

reasoning.objective: Infer how replacing or adding a vector affects whether a set is a basis, with a justified concrete claim.
misconceptions: adding a vector always improves a basis
any replacement preserves spanning and independence

meaning.objective: Recognize orthogonality from a zero inner product and distinguish it from linear independence.
misconceptions: orthogonal means normalized
independent vectors are always orthogonal

application.objective: Calculate a dot product or a scalar parameter that makes two nonzero concrete vectors orthogonal.
misconceptions: equating components instead of the dot product
ignoring signs in the dot product

reasoning.objective: Identify a valid argument that nonzero mutually orthogonal vectors are linearly independent, including the role of nonzero norms.
misconceptions: the zero vector may be included without affecting independence
orthogonality means all coefficients in every combination are zero
